newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Bank Austria board approves bid for Creditanstalt.
newsitem.headline: Bank Austria board approves bid for Creditanstalt.

text.p: Bank Austria's supervisory board has cleared the way for the management to submit a bid for Austria's second biggest bank, privatisation candidate Creditanstalt-Bankverein, Bank Austria said on Wednesday.

In a statement, released after a supervisory board meeting, Bank Austria said the decision to bid for the state's 70 percent of Creditanstalt ordinary voting shares was unanimous and would remain valid for a period of several months.

It gave no details of the bid, which Finance Minister Viktor Klima has said must be submitted by December 16. Austrian media have reported Bank Austria is ready to put up 16 billion schillings ($1.48 billion) for its rival.
Bank Austria spokesman Heimo Hackel said earlier that the bank's failure to take part in a due diligence process, which ended earlier this month, presented no obstacle to the bid.
"You can safely assume that we have looked into this matter thoroughly," Hackel told journalists.
Bank Austria, the nation's biggest bank, joins a consortium of industrialists and financial interests around insurer EA-Generali as the second public bidder for Creditanstalt.
The consortium has reportedly bid 720-730 schillings for two thirds of the state's 19.9 million ordinary shares. A Bank Austria bid of 16 billion schillings would work out at 804 schillings a share.
Creditanstalt ordinaries closed at 719.5 schillings on Wednesday. ($1=10.85 Schilling)
